**4. A page that opens or reloads a run after the deck attached never learns the deck is there — and then silently ignores every press.**
`tellWhoIsAttached` fires only on a tool's hello (`ws.ts:296`), a control/deck disconnect (`:244,247`) and a deck's watch (`:656`). It never fires when a *page* watches (`:651`). So: deck watches s1 → page reloads (F5 mid-stream) → page comes back with `decks = 0` → on an unshared run `publishing` is false → `RunView.tsx:447` returns early → presses are forwarded by the server, nobody subscribes, no `drove` is ever sent, and the deck's key hangs with no error anywhere. Same for opening the run after the deck picked it. Fix (one line): call `await tellWhoIsAttached(m["id"])` for every watcher joining, not just a deck — it also fixes the Attached panel missing a tool after a reload. And belt: drop `publishing` from the drive-effect gate at `:447`; `currentOffer` is computed unconditionally and already answers `needsPage`, so the page holding the run should always answer a press.

**5. A press can go unanswered three ways, and nothing in the wire times out.**
Besides #4: (a) a page that leaves the run for the library keeps its `WATCH#` row — `socket.ts:169` sends nothing for `watch(null)` and there is no unwatch message — so `heldRuns` still reports the run held, the press is forwarded to a page with no `RunView` mounted, and nothing replies; (b) `deps.store.getSession` or `deps.entitled` rejecting throws past the `drive` branch to the handler's catch (`ws.ts:~690`), returning 500 with no `drove`. `docs/stream-api.md` promises a verdict for every press. Fix: wrap the drive branch's store/entitlement reads so a failure becomes `refuse("Could not check that right now.")`, and document a client-side timeout (the plugin will need it regardless).

**6. The deck's only source of `seq` lags the page by the sync settle, so the second press in ~2s is refused.**
The `changed` doorbell carries `meta.seq`, the server's event count, which only advances after the sync push (`SyncProvider` settles 2000ms). A press lands, the page moves to N+1, the deck still holds N until the push — every press inside that window answers "That moved on.". The `drove` verdict is the obvious carrier for the new seq and currently carries none (`socket.ts` `drove(to, ref, ok, say)`). Decide this before Plan B builds a follow key on top of it; a human pressing Enter in `scripts/drive.ts` and reading the output takes longer than 2s, which is why Task 11's live check would not have surfaced it.

**7. The test that pins the live Lambda's gate env passes for the wrong reason.**
`hosted/infra/test/api.test.ts:112-124` matches any function with `WS_ENDPOINT` + `RUNLOG_GATES` + `STRIPE_FEATURES`. `WS_ENDPOINT` is set on the API handler (`api-stack.ts:566`) and the Discord job (`:568`) as well as the live handler (`:572`), and the API handler already had the other two (`:222,224`). Delete `api-stack.ts:461-462` and this test still passes — the one thing that would make the gate inert on deploy is unguarded. Fix: pull `template.findResources("AWS::Lambda::Function")`, find the entry whose logical id starts with `LiveHandler`, and assert on that resource's env.

**8. A deck that switches runs leaves the old page publishing forever.**
`ws.ts:651-657` tells the new run's table, and `$disconnect` (`:247`) tells only `leaving.run`, the last one. The stale `WATCH#` row for run A is never recomputed, so A's page stays at `decks = 1`, keeps `publishing` on, and keeps PUTting snapshots of an unshared run for nobody until it is remounted. The ledger accepts "keep publishing after the deck leaves" for the toast; this is the broader version. Fix: capture `conn.run` before the re-connect and `tellWhoIsAttached(previous)` when it differs.

**9. The act map has no automated coverage at all.**
`RunView.tsx:447-494` is where three of the branch's Important findings lived, and `RunView.offer.test.tsx` never emits a `{ t: "drive" }` on `syncBus`. One test — emit a drive for the rendered run, assert `sync.drove` was called and that the log grew by the expected event — would pin the seq source, the act wiring and the verdict return in one go.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)

- `RunView.tsx:287`: `subjectSuggestions(pack, run.state)` drops the `constrainedBy` argument the page passes (`:1540`), so the offer's suggestions are wider than the page's. Pass the active step's `constrainedBy`.
- `RunView.tsx:2180`: the Attached panel's trailing "Listening, so what the dice say happens in the game. Results still read the same with nothing attached." is tool copy, now shown on a deck-only panel where it is untrue.
- `offer.ts:85`: `owed > 0` withholds even a plain `rollTable` primary (`owed` is `blockingObligations`, unrelated to the step's `extraRolls`), so the follow key goes dead whenever anything is owed anywhere. Conservative and defensible — worth a line in `docs/stream-api.md` so the plugin's key face can say why.
- The publish effect now also re-fires on `receipts.length`/`activeStep`/`pending` changes via `currentOffer`, and every `putSnapshot` rings `changed` to all watchers (`api.ts:2690`), which makes every watcher pull. Roughly doubles the doorbell rate per roll.
- `ws.ts:660`: `tellDecks` runs a `decksOf` query on every watch and every disconnect for every account, deck or not; `heldRuns` is 1 + up to 20 queries per push. Bounded, but it is new cost on a hot path.
- `takePress.ts:60`: a thrown `Error`'s `message` goes straight onto a key face, so an internal `TypeError` text would reach an external client. Tag the intentional ones.
- `memoryLive.connect` keeps previous marks when called with no `attached`; `dynamoLive`'s `PutCommand` replaces the item. Only the deck's re-connect exercises it today.
- No negative test that the publisher stays off with neither `shared` nor a deck — the widened gate would pass its tests if it were always true.
- `activeStepLabel` (`RunView.tsx:76`) is the third copy of the step-heading switch (StepPanel, RemoteStep). It only produces a label, but the label is what a key face promises.

You are implementing the final-review fix wave on branch `the-deck-drives` (HEAD 9c4bb4f). Every task on the branch passed its own review; a whole-branch review then found one Critical and eight Important findings at the seams between tasks. You own all of them in one pass. Work from C:\Users\xbox\ScrtGit\sbm-ui. Bash tool with POSIX syntax is available.

## What the branch does (one paragraph, so the findings make sense)

An outside client with no engine of its own attaches to the hosted WebSocket as a **deck** (`?token=<jwt>&as=deck`, `hosted/infra/lib/handlers/ws.ts`), is pushed `{ t: "runs" }` (runs a browser page is holding — a **writing connection**: signed in, not `control`, not `deck`; predicate `writes()`), watches one, and sends `{ t: "drive", run, seq, ref, press, move?, answer? }`. The server forwards it to writing connections; the page holding the run (`apps/web/src/run/RunView.tsx`, the drive effect ~line 447, using the pure `apps/web/src/run/takePress.ts`) checks `seq` against its `run.events.length`, presses the same `useRun` function its own button would, and replies `{ t: "drove", to, ref, ok, say? }`, which the server routes back to that deck. The page publishes what may be pressed as `offer` (`apps/web/src/run/offer.ts`, `offerOf`) beside its snapshot, gated on `publishing = shared || decks > 0`; `decks` comes from the server's `tools` gesture (`tellWhoIsAttached`), read by `useAttachedDecks`. The live store (`hosted/infra/lib/handlers/live.ts`, `dynamoLive`, and the `memoryLive()` double in `hosted/infra/test/ws.test.ts`) is two-row: a CONN row per connection, a watch row per (session, connection); `watchers(sessionId)` reads the watch rows. `scripts/drive.ts` is a headless proof and `docs/stream-api.md` documents the wire in a section "Driving a run from a deck".

Read the ledger's final-review block for context if you want it: C:\Users\xbox\ScrtGit\sbm-ui\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-14-the-deck-drives-plan-a\progress.md (the lines beginning `- FINAL REVIEW`).

## The findings and the controller's ruling on each — implement exactly these

**C1 (Critical) — a press is applied once per device holding the run.** `ws.ts` (~477, 491): `writers` is every watcher passing `writes()`, and the press is posted to all of them — the owner's second device, and another member's browser, all apply it; the co-player's device then authors the event and its `drove` is dropped (~522, `target.sub !== conn.sub`). Ruling: (a) `live.ts` — the watch row stores the `at` that `watch()` already receives as `watchedAt`, `watchers()` returns `watchedAt` on each `Watcher`; `memoryLive` does the same. (b) `ws.ts` — `writers` = watchers passing `writes()` **and** `w.sub === conn.sub`, sorted newest `watchedAt` first (ties by `connectionId`), and **exactly one** is taken (`slice(0, 1)`). Tests: two pages of the owner watching → one `drive` posted, to the newer; a second member's page watching → nothing posted to it; the "no writer" refusal still fires when only another member holds the run.

**I2 — `moves` and `undo` escape the `live` gate.** `offer.ts` (~69-72): `bare` carries `moves`/`undo` into the `!live` return, and `takePress`'s `move`/`undo` arms consult only those. Ruling: the `!live` branch returns `moves: []`, `undo: null`, `primary: null`, `needsPage: "Open the run on the page"`. Test.

**I3 — per-contestant moves are offered and pressed against the table.** `RunView.tsx` (~283) maps every `run.moves`; the page's `Moves` (~2325) renders one button per contestant when `move.per === "contestant"` and a roster exists, calling `takeMove(id, label, undefined, contestant)`. Ruling: filter beside `heldMove` exactly as `Moves` splits — a `per === "contestant"` move is not offered when the run has contestants (read the JSX for the precise condition and mirror it). Test in `RunView.offer.test.tsx` if the fixture can carry a roster; otherwise a unit test of the extracted predicate plus a note.

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## Step 1: Verify Tests

Run the project's full test suite (`npm test` / `cargo test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...`).

**If tests fail**, report the failures and stop — the menu comes after a green suite:

```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]
```

**If tests pass:** continue to Step 2.

## Step 2: Detect Environment

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:

| State | Menu | Cleanup |
|-------|------|---------|
| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |

## Step 3: Determine Base Branch

The base branch is whatever this work forked from — usually named in the
plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream. If it is not already
known, ask: "This branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"
Confirm before merging: merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo.

## Step 4: Present Options

**Normal repo and named-branch worktree — present exactly these 3 options:**

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Detached HEAD — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete. You're on a detached HEAD (externally managed workspace).

1. Push as new branch and create a Pull Request
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

Present the menu exactly as written — concise, with every option coming
from the list above. Discarding the work happens only in response to your
human partner explicitly asking for it (see "If your human partner asks to
discard the work" below). Wait for their answer; the integration decision
is theirs.

## Step 5: Execute Choice

### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Get main repo root for CWD safety
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"

# Merge first — verify success before removing anything
git checkout <base-branch>
git pull
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>
```

If tests fail on the merged result: stop, leave the worktree and branch in
place, and investigate — nothing has been pushed, so the merge is local
and recoverable.

Once the merged result is green: clean up the worktree (Step 6), then
delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
git push -u origin <feature-branch>
# From a detached HEAD, name the new branch on the remote:
# git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch>
```

Then create the pull/merge request against <base-branch> with the forge's
tooling — its CLI if one is available, or the creation URL most forges
print when you push — following the repo's PR template and conventions if
present, and report the URL to your human partner.

Keep the worktree — your human partner iterates on PR feedback there.

### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

### If your human partner asks to discard the work

This path exists only as a response to an explicit request to throw the
work away. Confirm first:

```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for that exact confirmation. When it arrives:

```bash
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"
```

Then clean up the worktree (Step 6) and force-delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

## Step 6: Cleanup Workspace

**Runs for Option 1 and confirmed discards.** Options 2 and 3 always
preserve the worktree. Both callers have already changed directory to the
main repo root — worktree removal must run from outside the worktree —
and use the `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON`/`WORKTREE_PATH` values captured in
Step 2, from before that directory change.

**If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON`:** Normal repo, no worktree to clean up. Done.

**If `WORKTREE_PATH` is under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`:** Superpowers
created this worktree — we own cleanup:

```bash
git worktree remove "$WORKTREE_PATH"
git worktree prune  # Self-healing: clean up any stale registrations
```

**If removal is refused** (`contains modified or untracked files`): the
worktree holds files that exist nowhere else — uncommitted plans, notes,
or scratch work. Never `--force` on your own initiative. Show your human
partner what is at stake and ask:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" status --porcelain -uall
```

```
Worktree removal refused — these files were never committed:

<file list>

1. Commit them to <branch> before cleanup
2. Move them into <main repo root>
3. Delete them (unrecoverable)

Which?
```

Carry out the choice, then remove the worktree.

**Otherwise:** The host environment owns this workspace — leave it in
place. If your platform provides a workspace-exit tool, use it.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | yes | - | - | yes |
| 2. Create PR | - | yes | yes | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | yes | - |
| Discard (explicit request only) | - | - | - | yes (force) |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Tests passed earlier this session" | Run the suite on the tree you are about to integrate. A green run only proves the tree it ran on. |
| "They obviously want it merged" | Integration is your human partner's decision. Present the menu and wait. |
| "They seem done with this feature — I'll offer to discard it" | The menu is complete as written. Discard happens only when your human partner asks for it in so many words. |
| "'Yeah, get rid of it' counts as confirmation" | Only the typed word `discard` authorizes deletion. |
| "The PR is up, so the worktree is clutter now" | PR feedback gets fixed in that worktree. It stays until the work lands. |
| "This other worktree looks stale — I'll clean it too" | Clean up only worktrees under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`. Everything else belongs to the host. |
| "Removal refused — `--force` is just finishing the cleanup" | The refusal means files exist only in that worktree. `--force` destroys them permanently. Show your human partner and ask. |
| "The merged-result failure is probably flaky" | A failing merged result stops everything. Branch and worktree stay put while you investigate. |
| "The base branch is obviously main" | Confirm the fork point or ask. Merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo. |
| "The push was rejected — force-push will fix it" | A rejected push means the remote moved. Investigate; force-push only on your human partner's explicit request. |

A signed-in client with no engine of its own can attach to the socket as a deck, hear which of the account's runs a page is holding, and press what that run is offering. The page stays the one writer: it publishes an `offer` beside its snapshot, takes a `drive`, presses the same function its own button would, and answers `drove`. Every press carries the `seq` of the offer it was drawn from and is refused as "That moved on." when the run has moved past it.

Design: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/442de4ff-fd8f-42fd-b511-ba7606b82e1b

## Server

- `?token=<jwt>&as=deck` attaches a deck; `runs` is pushed on connect and whenever the set of runs held by a writing device changes.
- A deck watches a run; the table is told (the `tools` gesture carries `decks`), on every watcher joining and when a deck leaves a run (`unwatch`).
- `drive` is forwarded to exactly one device: the owner's own, the one that watched the run most recently (`watchedAt`). `drove` is routed back to the deck that asked, with the run's new `seq`.
- Refusals from the server: not yours, ended, nothing holding it, cannot check right now, and "Driving a run from a deck is part of Plus." where plans are on. Watching is not gated.
- One entitlement check and one feature parser (`billing.ts`), shared by both handlers; the live function now carries the gate's environment.

## App

- `run/offer.ts`: what a deck may press — primary (roll, carry on, close, enter, by the engine's own `closesUnit`), moves the page would show, undo, `needsPage`, presets for a subject and for "tick everything and finish".
- `run/takePress.ts`: the pure driver — seq check, one press per `${from}:${ref}`, acts in try/catch.
- `RunView.tsx` publishes the offer, widens the publisher to a run with a deck on it, takes the press, holds an accepted verdict until the log grows so the `seq` it sends back is fresh.
- `Checklist.tsx` `ticksToFinish`: the keys a click would commit, settling-aware, off-list rows without the point's tally.
- The app's first toast, shown when a deck arrives; the deck listed where attached tools are.

## Proof

`scripts/drive.ts` (`npm run drive`) is a deck in sixty lines. `docs/stream-api.md` documents the wire under "Driving a run from a deck". Dev deploys from main, so the live check runs after this lands:


entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, indefinitely** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Timeout → killed. Set `persistent: true` for session-length watches (PR monitoring, log tails) — the monitor runs until you call TaskStop or the session ends. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms, max 3600000ms. Ignored when persistent is true.

persistent.description: Run for the lifetime of the session (no timeout). Use for session-length watches like PR monitoring or log tails. Stop with TaskStop.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

Where things stand:

- **#288 merged and deployed to dev** (`Deploy Dev` succeeded; the run shows `waiting` only because "Tag and publish" waits on the release gate, by design).
- **A bug of mine surfaced on the first live attempt:** `scripts/drive.ts` renewed the CLI session but never saved the rotated one, so one run after the hour was up left your saved session dead — that's the "lapsed" you'd have hit on the next `runlog` command. **#289** fixes it (the script now goes through the CLI's own `bearer`, which renews and saves), auto-merge armed: https://github.com/SCRT-HQ/runlog/pull/289. This checkout already has the fix.

To run the proof I need two things from you, both quick:

```
npm run runlog -- login --api https://runlog.dev.scrthq.com/api
```

and a reload of the `streamdeck-test` tab so it's on the new site build. Say when, and I'll run the deck: list first, then one press with you watching.

message.content: I've reauthenticated the CLI. Shouldn't we be caching refresh tokens to prevent having to reauthorize the device, considering it's device flow?

content.text:
Yes — and that's already how it works; the trip-up was my bug, not a missing cache. `runlog login` saves both tokens to the CLI's config file: the access token (one hour) and the refresh token (30-day inactivity on the CLI's WorkOS client). `bearer` renews silently when the access token is near expiry, and you never see the device flow again. What bit you is that WorkOS **rotates** the refresh token on every renewal — the old one is retired the moment the new one is issued — and my script renewed without writing the new pair back, so the file was left holding a dead token. With #289 the script saves what it renews, and one login should carry you for a month of use. Plan B's plugin keeps its own session file (`runlog-deck`, separate from the CLI's) for exactly this reason: two processes renewing one rotating token would race each other.

Now the proof. Server half first — no press, it just needs to be told which run you're holding:

content.text:
Second bug from the live check, and it's a better find than the first: **the deck's run list was pushed from inside `$connect`**, and API Gateway refuses a `PostToConnection` until `$connect` has returned — the 410 came back, `tellDecks` read it as "the deck has gone" and deleted its rows, so every deck attached to the deployed server was connected at the gateway and unknown to the server. Silent forever. The test suite's in-memory poster can't refuse a post, so no test on the branch could have caught it; only a real gateway does.

Your tab needs no second reload — the page half is unchanged. #289 (the session fix) is queued too.

content.text:
Plan A is complete, merged, deployed to dev, and proven against the real gateway. `main` is at `ecb2fc2` with all three PRs; the local branches were already pruned by the merge.

## What landed

| PR | Subject |
| --- | --- |
| #288 | `feat(live): a run can be driven from outside it` — 29 commits, 12 tasks, every one reviewed; one Critical and eight Importants from the whole-branch review fixed before merge |
| #289 | `fix(cli): the deck script keeps the session it renews` — found on the first live attempt |
| #290 | `fix(live): a deck is told its runs when it speaks, not at connect` — found on the second |

**Live on dev, tonight:** `hello` → `runs` in 270 ms · `watch` → the toast on your tab · a press with the doorbell's `seq` → `drove ok:true` with the new `seq` in ~600 ms and the run moved · a deliberately stale press → `"That moved on."` carrying the current `seq`. (Tell me what the tab did on that first press when you get a second — roll or enter — I'd like it in the record.)

## Rulings I made on your behalf

In order, each with what it costs if wrong. Everything here is reversible.

1. **Feature branch in the main working copy, not a worktree.** Your habit; nothing you haven't already accepted.
2. **No Claude trailers on any commit**, per your standing rule, over the harness's attribution guidance. A trailer can be added; a forbidden one can't be unpublished.
3. **A deck sends `watch` for the run it picked; the server re-writes its CONN row and tells the table.** Without it the page never learned a deck was on. One extra PUT per watch.
4. **Task 8 mirrors `needsPlus` exactly; `grantsOf` and `featuresFromEnv` extracted to `billing.ts`.** Same function, one spelling.
5. **Bus field `run`; `Acts.primary` dispatches on the offer's id** (roll → `begin`, carry-on → `completeStep`, close → `closeAndEnter`, enter → `enterUnit`). Caught by tests and the live run if wrong.
6. **`manual` with no checklist is a plain press; with items it needs the page; `finalizeUnit` with confirm items needs the page.** Hands-free's rule.
7. **`decksOf` tested on the memory double, not DynamoDB.** Same exposure as every other query in `live.ts`.
8. **`tellDecks`'s whole body inside one try** — a deck that can't be given its list is still connected. A swallowed store error shows as an empty picker, logged.
9. **The DynamoDB watch-row bug (Task 6's find) fixed in Task 7, with the test double made two-row-faithful.** Nil if wrong; it made the Task 4 test go red on its own.
10. **The live Lambda gets the gate env; one parser, not two.** One env var and one import.
11. **Between units, the offer carries "Enter Day N"; Finish stays on the page** (it's the Next/Finish fork, a decision). One input field.
12. **Task 9's three narrowings**: `close` routed by the engine's `closesUnit`, `answer` gated on a preset, held moves filtered; plus acts in try/catch and `seen` keyed by deck. Every change narrows a deck to what the page allows.
13. **Task 12 added mid-plan** for your tick-everything key, as a preset on a named key, never the follow key. One task; nothing downstream.
14. **The deck row lives in the `Attached` panel**, where tools are, not `Members`.
15. **`useToast` re-arms on identical text; one integration test for the note.** Nil.
16. **Off-list checklist rows are ticked tally-less, as the Constraints panel ticks them.** The tally arithmetic is proven against a real click.
17. **The headless script reads the CLI session and takes `seq` from the doorbell.** (Later corrected: it must *save* what it renews — #289.)
18. **Security review's "token in URL" flag acknowledged, no change** — it's the socket's existing contract; browsers and Node can't set the header.
19. **Final-review C1: one press lands on exactly one device — the owner's, newest `watchedAt`.** A press on the wrong one of your own devices is visible, not corrupting.
20. **`drove` carries the run's new `seq`, held until the log grows** (1500 ms fallback). Decided now so Plan B's follow key has it.
21. **Deferred with rulings, not fixed:** a page that leaves the run keeps its watch row (needs an unwatch on the wire); a retried `ref` waits on the timer; `tellWhoIsAttached` is chatty when a room reconnects; a future act's `TypeError` text could reach a key face.
22. **Kept the scratch workspace until the live check passed, then removed it.**
23. **A deck speaks first (`hello`); nothing ever posts from `$connect`.** Now a rule in memory.

## Not in the code, worth knowing

- `runlog login --api` wants the base **with** `/api` — that's what tripped your first login, and the CLI's error could say so.
- My shell's AWS profile isn't the dev account, so I couldn't read the live Lambda's log; not needed in the end.
- The main run for each merge sits at `waiting` on the release gate — that's "Tag and publish" waiting for its reviewers, by design.

## Next

Plan B — the plugin — is written at `.claude/plans/2026-09-14-the-deck-drives-plan-b.md` (local, gitignored, per your rule), thirteen tasks starting with the WorkOS deck client and `packages/session/`. Two amendments from tonight go into its first dispatch: the deck sends `hello` after connect, and the session store persists every renewal. Your Stream Deck gets its first real test at Task 10. Say when.

## Queries (7)
- apiKeys: List signing keys for an environment, optionally scoped by application and key state

- defaultAuthkitApplication: Return an application's customized AuthKit branding, or null when it inherits the environment's branding

- environmentApplications: List the Connect applications in an environment

You are implementing Plan B, Task 4: `packages/session/` — one device flow, two callers.

## Task Description

Read your task brief first — it is your requirements, with the exact values to use verbatim:
C:\Users\xbox\ScrtGit\sbm-ui\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-14-the-deck-drives-plan-b\task-4-brief.md

## Context

`packages/cli/src/account.ts` signs the CLI in with the WorkOS device flow and keeps a session (access token, rotating refresh token) in the user's config directory. A Stream Deck plugin (later tasks) needs the same flow and the same renewal arithmetic. This task moves the shared parts into a new workspace package `@runlog/session` that both import, so a security-relevant loop has one implementation. Nothing about the CLI's behavior or its saved files may change — an existing `runlog login` must keep working after this.

## Controller rulings that AMEND the brief

1. **Names.** The brief calls the renewal `refresh`; the CLI's function is `renew(session, deps)`. Keep `renew` — export it under that name; every `refresh` in the brief means `renew`.
2. **What moves.** From `account.ts`: `Session`, `FlowDeps`, `realDeps`, `DEVICE_GRANT`, `RENEW_MARGIN_MS`, `TokenAnswer`, `postForm`, `expiryOf`, `deviceFlow`, `renew` — verbatim, into `packages/session/src/flow.ts`. Add `needsRenewal(session, now)` as the brief shows. **The CLI's `bearer(creds, force, deps)` stays in the CLI** (it is `Credentials`-shaped, and Plan A's script imports it from there); it now calls the package's `renew` and, in place of its inline lapsing arithmetic, `needsRenewal`. `credentials()`, `save()`, `Credentials`, `credentialsPath` and the commands stay in the CLI.
3. **`configDir(app)` must give the CLI its exact current path.** The CLI's rule (`account.ts:59-66`) is: `RUNLOG_CONFIG_DIR` if set, else `%APPDATA%\runlog` on Windows (falling back to `~/AppData/Roaming`), else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/runlog` (falling back to `~/.config`). Note it does NOT use `~/Library/Application Support` on macOS — the brief's `store.ts` snippet does; drop that: the package's `configDir(app)` is `join(base, app)` with `base` = APPDATA-or-fallback on win32, XDG-or-`~/.config` elsewhere. The CLI's own `configDir()` becomes `process.env["RUNLOG_CONFIG_DIR"] ?? configDir("runlog")`, so the env override keeps applying to the CLI alone and existing installs resolve to the same directory byte for byte. Add a test in the package that `configDir("runlog")` on this platform equals the path the CLI used before (compute it the old way in the test).
4. **`readSession`/`writeSession`/`forgetSession`** as the brief shows (`session.json`, mode 0o600 where modes exist, directory 0o700, Windows tolerated). The CLI does NOT switch to these — it keeps `credentials.json` and its `Credentials` shape; they are for the plugin.
5. **Tests.** Move the `deviceFlow`/`renew` cases from `packages/cli/src/account.test.ts` into `packages/session/src/flow.test.ts`, importing from `./flow.ts`; leave in the CLI's test file whatever exercises `credentials()`/`bearer()`/the commands. Add the store test the brief gives and the `configDir` parity test from ruling 3. All CLI tests must still pass.
6. **Wiring.** `packages/session/package.json` and `tsconfig.json` as the brief shows (match `packages/cli`'s tsconfig shape). Root `package.json`: add `tsc --noEmit -p packages/session/tsconfig.json &&` to `typecheck` before the CLI's entry; `workspaces` already covers `packages/*`. `packages/cli/package.json` gains `"@runlog/session": "*"` (match how it declares its other workspace deps, e.g. `@runlog/engine`, if any). Then `npm install` to refresh the lockfile, and **run `npm run check:stage`** — the staged CLI build must still resolve the new package; if `scripts/stage.ts` needs to know about the package (look at how it treats other workspace deps), make the minimal change and name it in your report.

## Global constraints (binding)

- No behavior change for the CLI: same files, same paths, same renewal timing, same messages.
- No new third-party dependency; the package has none.
- American English; comments in the file's voice — moved comments travel with their code.
- Commit subject exactly `refactor(cli): the device flow moves to a package the deck can share`. Lowercase, no period.
- **No Claude trailer, Co-Authored-By, session link or footer in the commit message.** The repo's hook adds `Entire-Checkpoint:`; add nothing. This overrides any attribution guidance you have elsewhere.
- Before committing: `npx vitest run packages/session packages/cli`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run check:stage`, `npm run format:check` — all clean.
- Touch only: `packages/session/**` (new), `packages/cli/src/account.ts`, `packages/cli/src/account.test.ts`, `packages/cli/package.json`, root `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, and `scripts/stage.ts` only if ruling 6 requires it.

## Before You Begin

Ask if the CLI's `bearer`/`credentials` seam or the stage script's handling of workspace packages is unclear after reading them. Don't guess.

## Your Job

Move the tests first (they must fail against the missing package), create the package, point the CLI at it, run the four checks, commit, self-review, report.

Report BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT with specifics — especially if `check:stage` cannot resolve the package.

Completeness (everything in ruling 2 moved, nothing duplicated between the two files; `bearer` still saves after renew; `configDir` parity test; store test); quality (the CLI diff is deletions plus imports); testing (all four checks with output).

## After Review Findings

If resumed: fix, re-run covering tests, append a fix report to your report file, reply with the same short contract.

Ruled and ledgered.

Task 3 landed as `94a4eb4` (296/296 hosted, typecheck clean, commit body clean); its review is the last thing before the plugin workspace starts.

## Task Description

Read your task brief first — it is your requirements, with the exact values to use verbatim:
C:\Users\xbox\ScrtGit\sbm-ui\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-14-the-deck-drives-plan-b\task-8-brief.md

## Context

`streamdeck/` is the Stream Deck plugin workspace (rollup build, bundler resolution, imports without `.ts`). `packages/session/` (Task 4, on this branch, `@runlog/session`) exports `deviceFlow(clientId, issuer, deps?)`, `renew(session, deps?)`, `needsRenewal(session, now)`, `configDir(app)`, `readSession(dir)`, `writeSession(dir, session)`, `forgetSession(dir)`, and the `Session`/`FlowDeps` types — read `packages/session/src/index.ts` and `flow.ts`/`store.ts` for the exact signatures. The hosted API hands out the deck's WorkOS client via `GET /api/auth/deck` → `{ clientId, issuer }` (Task 3). This task gives the plugin its own session: sign in through the device flow, keep the session in a file of the plugin's own, and hand out a bearer that renews **and saves** when near expiry.

## Controller rulings that AMEND the brief

1. **Names.** The brief's `refresh` is `renew` — import and call `renew`.
2. **Saving is not optional.** WorkOS rotates the refresh token on every renewal; a renewal that is not written back kills the login (this was bug #289 in Plan A). The brief's `bearer` already calls `writeSession(sessionDir(), renewed)` — keep it, and add a test that proves it: after a `bearer()` that renews, `readSession(sessionDir())` returns the *new* refresh token.
3. **`Account.apiBase` defaults come from the caller** (Task 10's `plugin.ts` reads `RUNLOG_API`); this module takes `Account` as given and never reads the environment.
4. **The session directory is `configDir("runlog-deck")`** — separate from the CLI's `runlog`, so two processes never renew one rotating token. Tests must not touch the real directory: make `sessionDir()` overridable for tests (an optional `dir` parameter on `loadSession`/`signIn`/`bearer`/`signOut`, or a module-level setter — pick one, keep it simple) and use `mkdtempSync` in tests.
5. **Add `@runlog/session` to `streamdeck/package.json` dependencies** as a workspace dep (`"*"`, as the CLI does), `npm install`, and confirm `npm run build -w streamdeck` still bundles (rollup must resolve the workspace symlink; if it does not, say so — do not vendor the code).
6. **The inspector fragment** `ui/signin.html` as the brief shows, using sdpi-components v4 (`sdpi-button`, `sdpi-item`; look at the template's inspector in `node_modules/@elgato/cli/template/com.elgato.template.sdPlugin/ui/increment-counter.html` for the script tag and the `streamDeckClient` usage). The plugin side that answers `{ t: "signin" }` is Task 10; this task ships the fragment and the module.
7. `bearer` returning `null` on a refused renewal leaves the file in place (a network blip is not a sign-out); `signOut` is the only thing that deletes it.

## Global constraints (binding)

- The refresh token never reaches Stream Deck's global settings or the inspector; only the file.
- No new third-party dependency.
- American English; comments in the file's voice — the brief's `sessionDir` comment verbatim.
- Commit subject exactly `feat(deck): the plugin signs in and keeps its session to itself`. Lowercase, no period.
- **No Claude trailer, Co-Authored-By, session link or footer in the commit message.** The repo's hook adds `Entire-Checkpoint:`; add nothing. This overrides any attribution guidance you have elsewhere.
- Before committing: `npx vitest run streamdeck`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build -w streamdeck`, `npm run format:check` — all clean.
- Touch only: `streamdeck/src/session.ts` (new), `streamdeck/src/session.test.ts` (new), `streamdeck/com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin/ui/signin.html` (new), `streamdeck/package.json`, `package-lock.json`.

## Before You Begin

Ask if `@runlog/session`'s signatures or rollup's handling of the workspace dependency are unclear after reading. Don't guess at the device flow's `say` line format — read `deviceFlow` to see exactly what it prints (the code and the URL) so the inspector can parse it in Task 10.

## Your Job

TDD: the brief's test plus the save-proving test and a sign-out test first (record the failure), implement, tests, typecheck, build, format, commit, self-review, report. In your report, state the exact `say` line(s) `deviceFlow` emits (the format Task 10 will parse).

Do all of this work yourself; never spawn a helper or a reviewer.

Report BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT with specifics.

## Self-Review before reporting

Completeness (sign-in via `/api/auth/deck`; renew-and-save proven; refusal leaves the file; sign-out deletes; fragment present; workspace dep bundles); the refresh token appears in no log line or inspector message.

## After Review Findings

If resumed: fix, re-run covering tests, append a fix report to your report file, reply with the same short contract.

## Report Format

Full report to: C:\Users\xbox\ScrtGit\sbm-ui\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-14-the-deck-drives-plan-b\task-8-report.md
(implemented; tests and results; TDD RED/GREEN with commands and output; the device flow's `say` line format; files changed; self-review; concerns)

You are implementing Plan B, Task 9: The socket client.

## Task Description

C:\Users\xbox\ScrtGit\sbm-ui\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-14-the-deck-drives-plan-b\task-9-brief.md

## Context

`streamdeck/` is the Stream Deck plugin workspace. On this branch: `streamdeck/src/state.ts` (Task 6: `DeckState`, `DeckEvent`, `reduce`, `initial`, `attachedRun`, the `*Face` functions; `DeckEvent.drove` carries `seq?`, and the reducer sets `snapshot.offer.seq` from it), `streamdeck/src/session.ts` (Task 8: `Account { apiBase }`, `bearer(account): Promise<string | null>` that renews and saves, `loadSession`, `signIn`, `signOut`). The server (Plan A, deployed): a deck opens `wss://<host>/ws?token=<jwt>&as=deck`, **sends `{ t: "hello" }` first**, and is answered with `{ t: "runs", runs: [...], any }` — pushed again whenever the held set changes; it sends `{ t: "watch", id }` for the run it picks and then hears `{ t: "changed", id, seq }`; it presses with `{ t: "drive", run, seq, ref, press, move?, answer? }` and hears `{ t: "drove", ref, ok, say?, seq? }`. The snapshot (with `offer` inside) is read over HTTP: `GET <apiBase>/api/sessions/<id>/snapshot` with a bearer (Task 2). This task adds `streamdeck/src/store.ts` and `streamdeck/src/socket.ts` (`openWire`), tested against a fake `WebSocket` and a fake `fetch`.

## Controller rulings that AMEND the brief

1. **Hello first.** In `ws.onopen`, after dispatching `socket: "open"`, send `JSON.stringify({ t: "hello" })`. The first test's assertion gains: `FakeSocket.last.sent[0] === JSON.stringify({ t: "hello" })` before the `watch`. Nothing is expected at connect without it.
2. **`drove` carries `seq`.** The `drove` branch dispatches `{ t: "drove", ref, ok, say?, seq? }` — `seq` only when `typeof m.seq === "number"`. A test: a `drove` with `seq: 5` after a snapshot with `offer.seq: 1` → `store.state.snapshot.offer.seq === 5` (the reducer already does this; the wire must pass it).
3. **`any`** — parse `m.any === true` into the `runs` event as the brief shows.
4. **Node's global `WebSocket`** — no `ws` import; `realDeps()` uses `globalThis.WebSocket`. Type it as `typeof WebSocket` (Node 22+ ships the global and its types via `@types/node` — if the workspace's tsconfig lacks the `dom` lib and the global is missing from types, add `"types": ["node"]` to `streamdeck/tsconfig.json` and say so).
5. **The bundle must transform the workspace package.** `rollup.config.mjs`'s `@rollup/plugin-typescript` (or whatever the template uses) does not transform `packages/session/src/*.ts`, so importing the session module into the bundle breaks `npm run build -w streamdeck`. Widen the TypeScript plugin's `include` (the template's config passes options — add `include: ["src/**/*.ts", "../packages/**/src/**/*.ts"]` or the equivalent that makes rollup transform workspace sources), then **prove it**: add to `streamdeck/src/plugin.ts` a module-level `export const store = makeStore();` and `export const wire = openWire({ apiBase: process.env["RUNLOG_API"] ?? "https://runlog.scrthq.com" }, store);` (no `connect()` call yet — Task 10 wires the lifecycle), so the import graph now includes `session.ts` → `@runlog/session`, and `npm run build -w streamdeck` must succeed. Keep those two lines exactly — Task 10 builds on them.
6. Reconnect backoff as the brief's `backoffMs`; a closed socket while `wanted` retries; `disconnect()` stops it.

Everything else — `Store`/`makeStore`, `WireDeps`, `Wire`, `openWire`'s `follow`/`fetchSnapshot`/`press`, the `sd-<time>-<rand>` ref, the four tests with the `FakeSocket` — as the brief shows. Tests use `vi.stubGlobal`-free injection (`deps.WebSocket`, `deps.fetch`, `deps.bearer`) as written.

- `press()` returns the `ref` it sent, or `null` when no run is attached, no `offer.seq` is known, or the socket is not open.

- Touch only: `streamdeck/src/store.ts` (new), `streamdeck/src/socket.ts` (new), `streamdeck/src/socket.test.ts` (new), `streamdeck/src/plugin.ts` (the two exports), `streamdeck/rollup.config.mjs` (the include), `streamdeck/tsconfig.json` only per ruling 4.

content.text:
Short answer: the URL, yes — but as a setting, not a key; connect/disconnect, no key either — as buttons in the inspector. Reasoning:

**The address needs a home, and I'd left it in the wrong place.** The plan reads the server from `RUNLOG_API` in the environment, which works for `npm run drive` and is useless for a plugin the Stream Deck app launches — there is no environment to set. Two real users need a non-default address: you, pointing at dev, and anyone running their own copy (the docs already promise a self-hosted copy answers at its own address). So it becomes a **"Runlog address"** field in the account block every inspector already shares (`signin.html`), default `https://runlog.scrthq.com`, kept in global settings — it's not a secret. The socket derives its `wss://` from it.

**Connecting is not a decision, so it shouldn't be a key.** The spec's rule is that the socket follows *configuration*: signed in plus at least one key placed means connected, always — because a plugin that only connects when someone remembers to press Connect never learns that a run started, and can never switch the deck to its profile. A Connect key would reintroduce exactly that failure. What people actually reach for is narrower:

- *"It's stuck"* → a **Reconnect** button in the inspector (drops and reopens the socket).
- *"Stop driving this run"* → **none** as a choice in the Run key's picker (unpins, keys fall back to "Pick a run" / "No run open").
- *"Forget my sign-in"* → **Sign out**, beside Sign in.

Three buttons in the inspector cost a streamer nothing; a Connect/Disconnect action costs one of a Mini's six keys for something they'd press twice a year. I'll add all three plus the address field to Task 10's inspector work (the plugin side of `signin.html`) and the "none" choice to Task 11's picker. If you do want a physical key for it after living with the inspector version, that's a one-action addition later.

"https://runlog.scrthq.com" }, store);` with no `connect()`, and `npm run build -w streamdeck` succeeding with the session module in the bundle; (6) backoff, retry while wanted, `disconnect()` stops.

The server's wire (Plan A, deployed) that the client must match exactly: connect `wss://<host>/ws?token=<jwt>&as=deck` → send `{ t: "hello" }` → receive `{ t: "runs", runs: [{ id, name?, packTitle?, held: true }], any }` (again on every change) → send `{ t: "watch", id }` → receive `{ t: "changed", id, seq }` for that run → `GET <apiBase>/api/sessions/<id>/snapshot` with `authorization: Bearer <token>` → send `{ t: "drive", run, seq, ref, press, move?, answer? }` → receive `{ t: "drove", ref, ok, say?, seq? }`.

Global constraints that bind this task:
- No `ws` dependency; no SDK import in `store.ts`/`socket.ts`.
- `press()` returns the `ref` it sent, or `null` when no run is attached, no `offer.seq` is known, or the socket is not open.
- Every outgoing frame is exactly one of the shapes above; nothing else is ever sent.
- The brief's `openWire` comment verbatim; American English.

- Touched only: `streamdeck/src/store.ts`, `streamdeck/src/socket.ts`, `streamdeck/src/socket.test.ts`, `streamdeck/src/plugin.ts`, `streamdeck/rollup.config.mjs`.

message.content: my thought around an explicit connect/disconnect button would be to prevent the WSS connection from effectively always being open, since people typically have their Stream Decks connected 24/7

content.text:
That's a better reason than "convenience," and it changes my answer. Let me put numbers on it first, then the design.

**What always-on actually costs.** API Gateway WebSocket bills connection-minutes (~$0.25 per million) and messages; a deck open around the clock is ~43,000 minutes a month — about a cent. But the gateway also hard-closes every connection at two hours, so an always-on deck reconnects ~360 times a month, and each reconnect is a `$connect` Lambda, a `hello`, a manifest read and up to twenty watcher queries for `heldRuns`, plus a fresh set of two-hour live rows in DynamoDB. Per deck it's pennies; at a thousand installs it's real money and, more to the point, it's a fleet of idle sockets doing nothing useful 23 hours a day because a Stream Deck never sleeps. You're right that "connected whenever configured" is the wrong default for hardware that's never off.

**So: a Connect key, and "on" is a state the streamer enters.** I'd reverse the earlier ruling this way:

- A sixth action, **Connect** — a toggle. Face reads *Offline* / *Connecting* / the attached run's name. Press to connect (sign-in, `hello`, runs, attach, and the profile switch all follow from that one press, which is a nicer "I'm streaming Runlog now" gesture than an automatic switch anyway); press again to disconnect. It's the key that lives on your main profile.
- While "on", the plugin reconnects through drops as it does now. While "off", it holds no socket and refreshes no token.
- **Idle auto-off**: if no run has been held for 30 minutes, the plugin disconnects itself and the key reads *Idle · press to connect*. That's the guard against "I pressed Connect at noon and forgot." 30 minutes is my pick; say if you'd rather 15 or 60.
- Every other key, while off, reads *Press Connect* — a new dim state — instead of pretending to be live.

What this gives up: the deck can't learn a run started while it's off, so no profile switch until you press. I think that's the right trade; it also removes the "Runlog keys in a background profile" problem entirely, because Connect is on the profile you're looking at.

The address field, Reconnect and Sign out stay in the inspector as before (Reconnect becomes "off then on"). I'll amend Task 10 to build Connect and the lifecycle around it and update the spec's "When the plugin connects" section on the artifact when the branch lands. Objections, or a different idle window?

content.text:
Both taken.

**Security.** Agreed — an idle deck holding an authenticated socket is a standing session on a device people leave plugged in; making "connected" something you enter and leave is the right posture, and the address stays account-level, never a run's, so nothing about it changes night to night.

**The off-state copy.** Your instinct is right that the key should say *what to do*, not just what's wrong. The constraint is the face: about ten characters a line at a size you can read from a chair, three lines at most — "Disconnected" alone is twelve and would get cut to "Disconnec…". So I'd render it in two parts the face already has: the title **"Not connected"** (wraps to two clean lines) and the small line beneath it, **"press Connect"** — state on top, the action under it. The Connect key itself reads **"Offline"** when off and **"Idle · press to connect"** after an auto-off. If "Disconnected" is the word you want, it fits as the small line instead: title "Press Connect", under-line "Disconnected". Say which reads better to you; I've put the first in the brief.

You are implementing Plan B, Task 10: The actions — the point where every module built so far meets the Stream Deck SDK.

## Task Description

Read your task brief first — it is your requirements, with the exact values to use verbatim:
C:\Users\xbox\ScrtGit\sbm-ui\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-14-the-deck-drives-plan-b\task-10-brief.md

**Read it to the end.** A section headed "Controller amendments (2026-09-14 21:35)" at the bottom overrides the task text above it where they differ: the socket lifecycle is no longer "connect when configured" but a **Connect action** the streamer toggles (with a 30-minute idle auto-off), the server address is a global setting rather than an environment variable, and the shared inspector block gains Sign out and Reconnect. The amendments carry the exact strings, UUID, state fields, and hardware sequence.

## Context

## Task Description

C:\Users\xbox\ScrtGit\sbm-ui\.superpowers\sdd\2026-09-14-the-deck-drives-plan-b\task-11-brief.md

## Context

`streamdeck/` is the Stream Deck plugin workspace. On this branch (HEAD d10fadc) Task 10 landed the six actions: `src/actions/base.ts` (`RunlogAction` with `face()`, `draw`, `send`, one store subscription per class), `src/actions/run.ts` (draws `runFace`, no `onKeyDown` yet), `src/plugin.ts` (`store`, `wire`, `turnOn`/`turnOff`, global settings cache with `apiBase` and `pinned`, `readGlobals`, the `onSendToPlugin` handler for `signin`/`signout`/`reconnect`, `sayWho`), `src/state.ts` (`attachedRun`, `runFace`, `DeckEvent.pin`), the shared inspector script `com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin/ui/account.js` loaded by every inspector page, and `ui/run.html`. Read those before writing; match their idioms (the SDK names Task 10 verified: `streamDeck.profiles.switchToProfile(deviceId, name)`, `streamDeck.devices`, `ev.action.device.id`, `streamDeck.ui.sendToPropertyInspector`, `streamDeck.settings.setGlobalSettings`). 1. **The picker gets "none."** The Run key's inspector lists the held runs by name and pack, with a first choice `none` (unpin: `pin(null)` → the deck follows again, or reads "Pick a run"/"No run open" as the state says). Pressing the key cycles through held runs exactly as the brief's `nextPin` does; the inspector is the authoritative picker.
2. **The profile switch is code-complete but the profile file comes later.** `streamDeck.profiles.switchToProfile(d.id, "Runlog")` on the change from no attached run to one, wrapped in `.catch(() => {})` as the brief shows, and the `PROFILE_NAME = "Runlog"` constant in one place. **Do not add the `Profiles` entry to the manifest** — `streamdeck validate` refuses one without the `.streamDeckProfile` file, and that file can only come from the user exporting their laid-out profile from the Stream Deck app. Leave a short comment beside the constant saying the manifest gains `Profiles: [{ Name: "Runlog", DeviceType: 0, Readonly: false, DontAutoSwitchWhenInstalled: true }]` when `profiles/Runlog.streamDeckProfile` is added. ## Global constraints (binding)

- `nextPin` pure and tested as the brief's three cases; `pin()` writes the setting and dispatches, nothing else.
- Faces via `runFace` unchanged; `showOk()` after a cycle press; `showAlert()` when there is nothing to cycle.
- No auto-connect; nothing here touches `turnOn`/`turnOff`.
- American English; comments in the file's voice — the brief's `Run` doc comment verbatim.
- Commit subject exactly `feat(deck): the run key picks, pins, and brings the deck to the runlog profile`. Lowercase, no period.
- **No Claude trailer, Co-Authored-By, session link or footer in the commit message.** The repo's hook adds `Entire-Checkpoint:`; add nothing. This overrides any attribution guidance you have elsewhere.
- Before committing: `npx vitest run streamdeck`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build -w streamdeck`, `npx --workspace streamdeck streamdeck validate com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin`, `npm run format:check` — all clean. **No plugin restart.**
- Touch only: `streamdeck/src/actions/run.ts`, `streamdeck/src/actions/run.test.ts` (new), `streamdeck/src/plugin.ts`, `streamdeck/com.scrthq.runlog.sdPlugin/ui/run.html`, and `ui/account.js` only if the `pin` message must route through it.

message.content: oh wow, as soon as I focused my browser tab, the buttons came alive and the run appeared in the list. Should the run list show all active runs (not just live/open runs), where selecting one makes it "live"/open without having to have Runlog open itself?

content.text:
That "as soon as I focused the tab" is worth understanding, because it'll bite a streamer: the tab had been open since 19:19, and Chrome discards or freezes tabs it thinks are idle (Memory Saver, and the intensive throttling that kicks in after a few minutes in the background). The page's live rows also expire after two hours. So from the server's point of view nobody was holding the run until the tab woke on focus, reconnected, and re-sent its `watch` — at which point the deck was told within a second, exactly as designed. The streaming guide should say to keep the run in an OBS dock or a browser source (never discarded) or to exempt the site from Memory Saver; and the page could re-arm its hold on a timer rather than only on reconnect. Both go in the ledger as follow-ups.

**Should the picker list every active run and let the deck make one live?** The honest constraint: **the page is the one writer.** The deck has no engine — it can only press a run that a browser is holding, and there is no server-side engine for ordinary runs (only the Discord bot hosts runs server-side). So a run with no page can't be driven by anything.

But there's a bridge that gets you nearly what you're asking, without a page being open beforehand: **picking a run the deck can't reach opens it.** The plugin has `system.openUrl`; if the list carried every unended synced run with a `held` flag, choosing an unheld one would pin it *and open its address in your default browser* — Runlog loads, the page holds the run, the deck attaches, the keys come alive. Cycling the Run key through unheld runs would do the same. From the deck's side that's "select a run and it goes live"; what it actually does is open Runlog for you, which is the only way a run can be live.

I'd do it as a follow-up task: a small server change (`runs` carries the unheld ones too, `held: false`, same twenty cap) merged ahead like Tasks 1–3 were, and the plugin half in the picker and the Run key. Want it in Plan B now, after Task 13?

W=.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-14-the-deck-drives-plan-b && cat > "$W/task-14a-brief.md" <<'EOF'
### Task 14a: A deck rolls the dice the page is waiting on

Found live 2026-09-14 22:57. On a `rollTable` step the page's `begin()` ends in `awaiting` whenever the dice are the player's to throw, and in a hands-free unit the step starts itself on arrival — so the run holds `pending` with a roll request the moment the step is reached. `offerOf` treats any unsettled step as `needsPage`, and the follow key goes dim exactly when the streamer wants to roll. The page has a button for this moment — **Roll for me** in `apps/web/src/run/RequestPanel.tsx` (~144-151): `rollDice(request.dice, Math.random)` → `onAnswer(request.key, thrown.total, true, thrown.dice, thrown.seed)`, where `onAnswer` is the `answer` wrapper `RunView` passes to `RequestPanel` (`onAnswer={answer}`, ~956), which also records the receipt and sends the `rolled` gesture. The deck presses that button.

**Files:**
- Modify: `apps/web/src/run/offer.ts`, `apps/web/src/run/offer.test.ts`
- Modify: `apps/web/src/run/RunView.tsx` (the `currentOffer` inputs and the drive effect's `primary` act)
- Modify: `apps/web/src/run/RunView.offer.test.tsx` (one integration case if the fixture can reach a pending roll; else say why)
- Modify: `docs/stream-api.md` (one sentence under the offer's `primary`: while the page waits on a roll, `primary` is the roll and pressing it rolls the app's dice)

**Interfaces:**
- `OfferInput` gains `request: { kind: "roll"; label: string } | { kind: "other" } | null` — the page derives it from `run.pending?.request`: `kind === "roll"` → `{ kind: "roll", label: request.label ?? <the step label> }`; any other request kind → `{ kind: "other" }`; no pending → `null`.
- `offerOf`: after the `live` check and before the typed/owed branches, when `!input.settled`: `request?.kind === "roll"` → `primary: { id: "roll", label: request.label, kind: "rollTable" }`, `needsPage: null` (moves/undo as they are); otherwise the existing unsettled `needsPage`. The settled paths are unchanged.
- `RunView`'s `Acts.primary`, `roll` case: if `run.pending?.request?.kind === "roll"`, do exactly what Roll for me does — `rollDice(run.pending.request.dice, Math.random)` and `answer(run.pending.request.key, thrown.total, true, thrown.dice, thrown.seed)` through the same `answer` wrapper (import `rollDice` from where `RequestPanel` does); otherwise `run.begin(...)` as today. No other act changes.
- `takePress.ts` unchanged.

**Steps:**
1. Tests first: `offer.test.ts` — unsettled + `request: { kind: "roll", label: "Draw a curse" }` → `primary` equals `{ id: "roll", label: "Draw a curse", kind: "rollTable" }` and `needsPage` null; unsettled + `{ kind: "other" }` → the existing needsPage; settled cases unchanged (add `request: null` to `base`). Run: FAIL.
2. Implement `offer.ts`.
3. `RunView.tsx`: the `request` input in `currentOffer`; the `roll` act branch. If `RunView.offer.test.tsx`'s fixture can put the demo run on a roll step with a pending request (drive `begin` on a rollTable step with auto-roll off), add a case: a `drive` press → the log gains the roll's events and `drove` is `ok: true`; otherwise state why and rely on the unit tests.
4. `npx vitest run apps/web/src/run && npm run typecheck && npm run lint:docs && npm run format:check`.
5. Commit: `fix(run): a deck rolls the dice the page is waiting on`. No trailer, no footer.

Branch: **`the-deck-rolls`, off `origin/main`** (not `the-deck-arrives`) — this ships ahead of the plugin, as PR with auto-merge, title `fix(run): a deck rolls the dice the page is waiting on` (`run` is an allowed scope).
EOF

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - User asked to plan and build an Elgato Stream Deck integration for Runlog: full run control from the deck (advance screens, trigger rolls) and widgets showing live metrics. Decisions made via questions: the host's own deck with the page's full power (not the ask tier); presses travel through the hosted server; "follow key" + named keys; typed steps via preset answers on named keys; sign-in inside the plugin (WorkOS device flow, client of its own); in-repo `streamdeck/` workspace shipped to the Elgato Marketplace; driving is part of Plus, watching not gated.
   - Spec is an artifact (user: artifacts are the record, not repo docs): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/442de4ff-fd8f-42fd-b511-ba7606b82e1b. Plans are local, gitignored files: `.claude/plans/2026-09-14-the-deck-drives-plan-a.md` and `-plan-b.md` (user: "it should remain local … .claude/* is gitignored intentionally").
   - User asked for: commits + PRs opened when work is done (conventional titles, no footer; ask before arming auto-merge — later chose "merge, then verify on dev"); a "tick everything and finish" key (Plan A Task 12); an explicit Connect/Disconnect (security + not holding a WSS 24/7) — adopted as a Connect toggle action with 30-min idle auto-off; off-state keys should say to connect first ("Not connected" / "press Connect"); a run-agnostic server address setting; the run picker to show all active runs and make one live (proposed Task 14: server sends unheld runs with `held:false`; picking one pins + `system.openUrl` opens it in the browser — awaiting user's answer); fix the live-found bugs: follow key dies at a roll step ("nothing allows me to actually Press to Roll") and Metric key displays nothing.
   - User also asked (side thread) to address VS Code "Cannot find name 'node:crypto'" ts(2591) errors — fixed by adding `"types": ["node"]` to cli/session/engine tsconfigs (commit 70d4cd4); user re-check pending.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Runlog: the page is the one writer; deck has no engine; server forwards `drive` to exactly ONE writing connection (owner's newest `watchedAt`); `drove` carries the run's new `seq`; `offer` block published in the snapshot by the page (`offer.ts`); `takePress.ts` pure driver (seq check, `${from}:${ref}` dedupe).
   - API Gateway WebSocket: cannot PostToConnection until `$connect` returns → deck must speak first (`{t:"hello"}`), answered with `{t:"runs", runs, any}`; 2-hour hard connection limit; live rows TTL 2h.
   - WorkOS device flow; refresh tokens ROTATE on renewal → anything that renews must persist (`bearer()` in packages/cli/src/account.ts; plugin's `session.ts` writes back).
   - Elgato SDK `@elgato/streamdeck` 2.1.2 pinned, Node 24 runtime, SD 7.1+ (user on 7.5.1); `setImage` base64 SVG data URI (raw SVG rejected on Windows); `switchToProfile` only to profiles shipped in the manifest; validator rejects "Neo" controller and caps Controllers at 2; `Profiles` manifest entry requires the `.streamDeckProfile` file (user must export their laid-out profile); sdpi-components v4 (`streamDeckClient.on` doesn't exist → `sendToPropertyInspector.subscribe`).

   - CI: dev deploys only from main; PR title scopes allow-list (run, designer, library, marketplace, profile, live, engine, schema, cli, packs, hosted, ci, docs, deps, deps-dev, release) — `api` not allowed (use `hosted`); `deck` to be added by the plugin PR.
   - SDD process: fresh implementer per task, task review, fix rounds, scoped re-reviews, ledger in `.superpowers/sdd/<plan>/progress.md` (gitignored).

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `hosted/infra/lib/handlers/ws.ts` — deck attach (`as=deck`), `writes()` predicate, `heldRuns` (returns `{runs, any}`), `tellDecks`, deck `hello` branch (`if (conn.deck && m["t"] === "hello") { await tellDecks(conn.sub, connectionId); return {statusCode:200}; }`), `drive`/`drove` routing, Plus gate `refuse("Driving a run from a deck is part of Plus.")`, `tellWhoIsAttached` counts `decks`, deck watch re-connects CONN row with `{deck:true, run}`, `unwatch` on run switch.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\xbox\.claude\plugins\cache\claude-plugins-official\superpowers\6.3.0\skills\finishing-a-development-branch

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

**Core principle:** Verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

## Step 1: Verify Tests

Run the project's full test suite (`npm test` / `cargo test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...`).

**If tests fail**, report the failures and stop — the menu comes after a green suite:

```
Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

[Show failures]
```

**If tests pass:** continue to Step 2.

## Step 2: Detect Environment

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:

| State | Menu | Cleanup |
|-------|------|---------|
| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |

## Step 3: Determine Base Branch

The base branch is whatever this work forked from — usually named in the
plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream. If it is not already
known, ask: "This branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"
Confirm before merging: merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo.

## Step 4: Present Options

**Normal repo and named-branch worktree — present exactly these 3 options:**

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Detached HEAD — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete. You're on a detached HEAD (externally managed workspace).

1. Push as new branch and create a Pull Request
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

Present the menu exactly as written — concise, with every option coming
from the list above. Discarding the work happens only in response to your
human partner explicitly asking for it (see "If your human partner asks to
discard the work" below). Wait for their answer; the integration decision
is theirs.

## Step 5: Execute Choice

### Option 1: Merge Locally

```bash
# Get main repo root for CWD safety
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"

# Merge first — verify success before removing anything
git checkout <base-branch>
git pull
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>
```

If tests fail on the merged result: stop, leave the worktree and branch in
place, and investigate — nothing has been pushed, so the merge is local
and recoverable.

Once the merged result is green: clean up the worktree (Step 6), then
delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -d <feature-branch>
```

### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
git push -u origin <feature-branch>
# From a detached HEAD, name the new branch on the remote:
# git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch>
```

Then create the pull/merge request against <base-branch> with the forge's
tooling — its CLI if one is available, or the creation URL most forges
print when you push — following the repo's PR template and conventions if
present, and report the URL to your human partner.

Keep the worktree — your human partner iterates on PR feedback there.

### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

### If your human partner asks to discard the work

This path exists only as a response to an explicit request to throw the
work away. Confirm first:

```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for that exact confirmation. When it arrives:

```bash
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"
```

Then clean up the worktree (Step 6) and force-delete the branch:

```bash
git branch -D <feature-branch>
```

## Step 6: Cleanup Workspace

**Runs for Option 1 and confirmed discards.** Options 2 and 3 always
preserve the worktree. Both callers have already changed directory to the
main repo root — worktree removal must run from outside the worktree —
and use the `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON`/`WORKTREE_PATH` values captured in
Step 2, from before that directory change.

**If `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON`:** Normal repo, no worktree to clean up. Done.

**If `WORKTREE_PATH` is under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`:** Superpowers
created this worktree — we own cleanup:

```bash
git worktree remove "$WORKTREE_PATH"
git worktree prune  # Self-healing: clean up any stale registrations
```

**If removal is refused** (`contains modified or untracked files`): the
worktree holds files that exist nowhere else — uncommitted plans, notes,
or scratch work. Never `--force` on your own initiative. Show your human
partner what is at stake and ask:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" status --porcelain -uall
```

```
Worktree removal refused — these files were never committed:

<file list>

1. Commit them to <branch> before cleanup
2. Move them into <main repo root>
3. Delete them (unrecoverable)

Which?
```

Carry out the choice, then remove the worktree.

**Otherwise:** The host environment owns this workspace — leave it in
place. If your platform provides a workspace-exit tool, use it.

## Quick Reference

| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
| 1. Merge locally | yes | - | - | yes |
| 2. Create PR | - | yes | yes | - |
| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | yes | - |
| Discard (explicit request only) | - | - | - | yes (force) |

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Tests passed earlier this session" | Run the suite on the tree you are about to integrate. A green run only proves the tree it ran on. |
| "They obviously want it merged" | Integration is your human partner's decision. Present the menu and wait. |
| "They seem done with this feature — I'll offer to discard it" | The menu is complete as written. Discard happens only when your human partner asks for it in so many words. |
| "'Yeah, get rid of it' counts as confirmation" | Only the typed word `discard` authorizes deletion. |
| "The PR is up, so the worktree is clutter now" | PR feedback gets fixed in that worktree. It stays until the work lands. |
| "This other worktree looks stale — I'll clean it too" | Clean up only worktrees under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`. Everything else belongs to the host. |
| "Removal refused — `--force` is just finishing the cleanup" | The refusal means files exist only in that worktree. `--force` destroys them permanently. Show your human partner and ask. |
| "The merged-result failure is probably flaky" | A failing merged result stops everything. Branch and worktree stay put while you investigate. |
| "The base branch is obviously main" | Confirm the fork point or ask. Merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo. |
| "The push was rejected — force-push will fix it" | A rejected push means the remote moved. Investigate; force-push only on your human partner's explicit request. |
